title: A Student interval with estimated spread

aliases: a student interval with estimated spread
purpose: How wide should a calibration interval be when the spread is estimated too?
meaning: Divide the sample standard deviation by the square root of the reading count. Use the Student multiplier with one fewer degree of freedom, then place the resulting margin on both sides of the observed mean.

definition.setting: A workshop checks the cutting error of a calibration jig. The recorded sample is summarized by its mean x̄, sample standard deviation s and number of readings n. Move s and watch the standard-error segment and the interval endpoints move together; change n to see both the square-root divisor and the Student multiplier change.

conditions: Assume independent readings from one normal population with unknown mean μ and unknown positive spread. The entered s is the sample standard deviation using n−1 in its variance denominator. Use n from 2 to 31, x̄ from −4 to 4 mm and s from 0.25 to 2 mm. Summaries are entered rather than newly sampled as a control changes. The fixed 95% procedure covers fixed μ in 95% of repeated samples under this model; it gives neither a posterior probability for one computed interval nor a prediction interval for the next reading. Unknown μ is not plotted. Student quantiles are numerical approximations, rather than rounded table values treated as exact.

examples.title: Ten readings with an estimated one-millimetre spread
examples.question: How wide should a calibration interval be when the spread is estimated too?

steps.reason: Keep the actual supplied summaries or constructed outcomes fixed as declared.

Divide the sample standard deviation by the square root of the reading count. Use the Student multiplier with one fewer degree of freedom, then place the resulting margin on both sides of the observed mean.
At n=10 the Student multiplier uses nine degrees of freedom. The margin is about 0.715 mm, giving endpoints about −0.215 and 1.215 mm.

examples.interpretation: At n=10 the Student multiplier uses nine degrees of freedom. The margin is about 0.715 mm, giving endpoints about −0.215 and 1.215 mm.
